title: Reference with plural personal pronouns and polite te
summary: Use me for the speaker’s group, te for listeners, and he for people being discussed; polite te retains plural agreement.
objectives: Use me for the speaker’s group, te for listeners, and he for people being discussed; polite te retains plural agreement.

sections.title: Follow the group’s role
paragraphs: Me includes the speaker and other people. Te normally addresses a group of listeners. He refers to several people being discussed.
He does not mark the gender of the people in the group.

sections.title: Polite te
paragraphs: Te can also address one person politely in formal situations. It still takes plural verb agreement.
Optional capitalization can show respect in some writing; it does not create a different pronoun.

steps: The speaker belongs to the group.
Check whether a group or one politely addressed person is listening.
The same pronoun te serves both uses and retains plural agreement.
The reference is a group of people.

commonMistakes: Do not use singular verb agreement with polite te.
Do not treat optional capitalization as a different pronoun.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Which pronoun fits two or more people who are being discussed?
practiceExercises.explanation: He is the third-person plural pronoun for a group of people.

optionFeedback.hän: “hän” does not fit this subject or construction. He is the third-person plural pronoun for a group of people.
optionFeedback.he: Correct. He is the third-person plural pronoun for a group of people.
optionFeedback.te: “te” does not fit this subject or construction. He is the third-person plural pronoun for a group of people.
